blocks.text: The desk is quiet before the day begins. Morning light reaches it first.
Focus is not a feeling you wait for. It is a place you return to, one small task at a time.
Benjamin Franklin wrote in Poor Richard's Almanack of 1748: "Lost time is never found again."
So begin with one thing. When your mind wanders, notice it, and come back.
The light moves across the desk as the hours pass. You are still here, still working.
